title: Perf harness expansion: golden workload suites, kernel selection benchmarks, and CI perf gates
creator: Avery Chen
description: Refactor and expand the internal benchmarking harness to provide reproducible golden baselines and CI performance gates targeting kernel selection, attention implementation variants, and prefill/decode scheduling. The current harness is ad-hoc, lacks coverage for rotary/ALiBi/Flash Attention permutations, and does not run representative workload suites used by customers (chat low-latency, high-throughput batch embeddings, long-context summarization). This ticket tracks design, implementation, and rollout of improved workload suites, golden baseline artifacts, automation for reproducible runs (seeded RNG, deterministic model weights where possible), and CI integration with thresholded gates and automatic regression alerts.
acceptance_criteria: A set of 6 workload suites (low-latency chat, multi-turn chat with KV reuse, high-throughput embeddings, long-prefill summarization, streaming decode stress, mixed-priority routing) implemented in the harness

Benchmarks that exercise kernel selection path: CPU fallback, quantized kernels, CUDA kernels with and without flash attention; measurable metrics for latency p50/p95, throughput (tokens/sec), and GPU utilization
Golden baselines committed to artifact store for three canonical models (gpt-like-7b, llama2-13b, and encoder-only embedding-2b) across short/medium/long seq lengths
CI perf gates added to mainline with clear thresholds and a rollback/fail strategy; regressions produce a JIRA/Linear issue and an alert to #perf-regressions Slack channel
Documentation and runbook published (Confluence link) describing how to add new workloads and update golden baselines
Grafana dashboards and dashboards links included in PRs; synthetic trace replayer integrated so CI runs can replay captured production traffic traces
tasks: Design workload taxonomy and mapping to kernel selection scenarios
Add ALiBi/rotary/position-bias toggle support to harness runners
Integrate flash attention binaries and fallback paths into CI containers
Implement deterministic RNG seeding and model snapshot pinning for golden runs
Create artifact naming convention and S3 layout for golden baselines
Add CI job templates with composite thresholds (latency + throughput + GPU memory) and mock alerting hooks
Build Grafana dashboards and validate with synthetic replayer traces
Author runbook and onboarding guide for engineers and SREs
notes: Initial spike showed up to 18% variance in p95 between different kernel choices when sequence length > 4k; prefill scheduling interacts with attention kernel selection causing tail latency spikes
We should avoid relying on absolute latency numbers across hardware; golden baselines will be tied to hardware profiles (A100-40GB, H100-80GB, T4) and Docker image tags
Decision: use two artifact channels - 'golden/locked' (immutable snapshots used for CI gates) and 'golden/experimental' (for candidate runs and maintained by perf owners)
Trade-off: running full workload suites in CI will increase pipeline time. Plan is to run lightweight 'smoke' suites on every push and a nightly full-suite run with historical comparison and alerting
We will include kernel-level metrics (kernel name, launch time, occupancy) exported from runtime to allow root-cause of regressions

implementation_plan: Week 1: finalize workload taxonomy, define golden baseline format, spike deterministic run reproducibility
Week 2-3: implement workload runners, integrate attention variant toggles, capture initial golden baselines for three models
Week 4: add CI job templates, add smoke and nightly jobs, wire alerts to Slack and create auto-open issue flow
Week 5: polish dashboards, author runbook, gather signoff from SRE and ML infra teams
Post-release: iterate on thresholds and expand hardware matrices
risks: CI runtime increase may slow developer velocity if smoke suite thresholds are too permissive or require frequent rebaseline
Hardware heterogeneity means golden baselines may diverge; mitigation: tie baselines to hardware tags and allow per-hardware thresholds
Determinism limits: some kernel optimizations are non-deterministic (e.g., cudnn heuristics); we need to capture variance windows rather than single number assertions
False positives in CI gates could block merges; need clear rollback and ephemeral disablement path
